defaults.title: Sensitive interface absent in non-secure contexts
defaults.behavior: A WebIDL interface or member marked [SecureContext] is not exposed in a non-secure context.
limitations: The classification of the context is delegated to HTML and Secure Contexts.

defaults.title: Untrustworthy origins fail trust-gated operations
defaults.behavior: An origin that the shared algorithm classifies as not potentially trustworthy does not satisfy a secure-context or trustworthy-origin precondition.
limitations: Potentially trustworthy is intentionally broader than public HTTPS origins.

defaults.title: Unspecified powerful-feature permission starts at prompt
defaults.behavior: If a powerful feature does not specify another default permission state, the Permissions specification uses `prompt`; expired permissions return to the feature's default state.

evidence.section: 4 Specifying a powerful feature: Default permission state

limitations: A feature may explicitly choose another state and user agents control prompt UX and grant lifetime.

defaults.title: Insecure or policy-disabled permission state is denied
defaults.behavior: The permission-state algorithm returns `denied` for a non-secure context or a Document not allowed to use the policy-controlled feature.
limitations: Only features integrated with Permissions Policy receive the policy-disabled branch.

defaults.title: Choose same-origin-only delegation for sensitive features
defaults.behavior: For a sensitive policy-controlled feature, prefer the `self` default allowlist so cross-origin child documents are disabled until explicitly delegated.
limitations: Permissions Policy defines `self` and `*` but does not impose `self` on every sensitive feature; applicability needs feature-specific justification.

defaults.title: CSP-protected inline execution is blocked without authorization
defaults.behavior: Under an applicable script policy, inline execution that does not match an allowed nonce, hash, or explicit unsafe source fails the inline check.
limitations: CSP is opt-in deployment policy; without a delivered policy this default is not active.

defaults.title: Enforced Trusted Types reject sink type mismatch
defaults.behavior: When `require-trusted-types-for` applies, a value that cannot be converted through the defined default-policy path is blocked from the protected sink.

evidence.section: 4.2.4 Should sink type mismatch be blocked?

limitations: Enforcement is CSP opt-in and does not establish that a Trusted Type policy is safe.

defaults.title: Mixed content is upgraded when eligible and otherwise blocked
defaults.behavior: The mixed-content algorithms first upgrade requests classified as upgradeable and block requests or responses that remain prohibited mixed content.
limitations: The exact resource categories and integration behavior can evolve with Fetch and HTML.

defaults.title: Declared insecure requests are rewritten before dispatch
defaults.behavior: When the client has an applicable upgrade-insecure-requests policy, eligible insecure requests are rewritten to a potentially secure URL before network dispatch.
limitations: The policy itself is opt-in and failed HTTPS upgrades are not silently retried over HTTP.

defaults.title: Integrity mismatch blocks protected resource use
defaults.behavior: When valid integrity metadata is present or required by Integrity Policy, resource bytes that do not match are not used.
limitations: Without metadata or an enforced Integrity Policy the resource is not integrity-pinned by SRI.

defaults.title: Credential retrieval is not ambient across ancestor origins
defaults.behavior: Credential operations evaluate same-origin-with-ancestors and mediation requirements; preventSilentAccess can force future mediation.
limitations: Specific credential types can define additional collection and mediation behavior.

defaults.title: Only in-scope eligible requests trigger DBSC refresh
defaults.behavior: A device-bound session refresh is attempted only after the request is associated with a session and satisfies the specification's scope and refresh-eligibility algorithms.

evidence.section: 8.3 Identify if a request is allowed to refresh

limitations: Server-provided scope instructions remain security-critical input and require independent constraints.

defaults.title: Use non-extractable, minimally scoped keys where export is unnecessary
defaults.behavior: When an application does not require raw key export, request a non-extractable CryptoKey and only the operations needed by the protocol.
limitations: WebCrypto makes extractability and usages explicit inputs; it does not universally default them to this recommendation.

defaults.title: Block a document incompatible with required policy
defaults.behavior: A response that cannot satisfy an embedder's required document policy is blocked by the Document Policy compatibility algorithm.

evidence.section: 9.7 Should response be blocked due to document policy?

limitations: This is editor-draft behavior for a charter deliverable still described as incubation.

defaults.title: Passkey endpoint discovery is HTTPS, same-RP, and non-redirecting
defaults.behavior: The well-known URL is constructed from `https`, the RP ID, a null port, and the fixed path; the server must not redirect.

evidence.source_title: A Well-Known URL for Relying Party Passkey Endpoints

limitations: The discovery response may omit workflow URLs by returning an empty JSON object.
